mainTopic: Saving an unborn baby on שבת, the hair of an executed woman, and the minimum and maximum payments for an ערך
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of שמואל's ruling that when a woman in labor dies on שבת, we cut her open to save the baby. רבה explains that the real news is that we may even carry a knife through רשות הרבים. The ruling is needed because an unborn baby never had a חזקה of being alive. Next the גמרא asks how the משנה can allow the hair of an executed woman, since a dead body is forbidden for benefit. רב says the 'hair' is a wig, which is allowed only if she said 'give it to my daughter'. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is her real hair: death forbids a woman, but the verdict forbids an animal. לוי brings a ברייתא supporting each view, and the first פרק ends. The new פרק teaches that an ערך is never less than one סלע or more than fifty. רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue whether a poor person with five סלעים pays one or all five, and the גמרא gives the פסוקים behind each side. Finally, רב אדא בר אהבה shows how a man with five סלעים can pay two ערך vows by paying the second vow first.

steps.title: Why say it? Cutting flesh is not a שבת problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling that we cut open a dead mother on שבת: that is only cutting flesh, so why would anyone think it is forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just cutting flesh!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge to שמואל's ruling about cutting open a mother who died in labor on שבת. It says that cutting dead flesh is not a real שבת violation, so the ruling seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting dead flesh is not one of the forbidden מלאכות of שבת. So permitting it should need no special teaching. The גמרא wants to know what new point שמואל was making.

phrases.english: He is merely cutting flesh!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge to שמואל's ruling from the previous section of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that we cut open a woman who died in labor on שבת to take out the baby.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting dead flesh is not a forbidden מלאכה, so the ruling teaches nothing new.

steps.title: The real point: carrying the knife through the public domain
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the ruling is needed to permit bringing a knife through רשות הרבים, which is a real Torah-level שבת violation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The ruling was only needed to allow bringing a knife through the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge. The new point is not the cutting but the carrying of the knife through רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying in רשות הרבים is a real Torah prohibition on שבת. שמואל teaches that we may even do this to try to save the baby. So the ruling is not obvious after all.

keyTerms.meaning: it was only needed for (the following case)
the public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden by the Torah

phrases.english: Rabba said: It was only needed
phrases.notes: He means: שמואל's ruling was only needed for the following point.

phrases.english: to bring a knife by way of the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the new point of the ruling to a different action (carrying, not cutting).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to be only about cutting flesh, which is obviously allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling teaches that we may even carry a knife through רשות הרבים on שבת to save the baby.

steps.title: We already know we break שבת even out of doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the point is that we break שבת even when it is unsure a life will be saved, a משנה about a rockslide already teaches that.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does this teach us? That we break שבת even out of doubt? We already learned: if a rockslide fell on someone, and we are unsure if he is there or not, alive or dead, a non-Jew or a Jew, we clear the pile off him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's answer. A משנה already teaches that we break שבת to save a life even when we are full of doubts, so why does שמואל need to teach it again?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby may already be dead, so carrying the knife is breaking שבת out of ספק. But the משנה of the rockslide already allows breaking שבת with three doubts together. So שמואל's ruling seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: we clear away the pile (of rubble)

phrases.english: And what does this teach us?
That out of a doubt we break Shabbat?
We already learned: one upon whom a rockslide fell,
phrases.notes: This משנה is in יומא 83a.

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק הוּא שָׁם, סָפֵק אֵינוֹ שָׁם,
phrases.english: it is unsure whether he is there, or not there,
unsure whether he is alive or dead,
unsure whether he is a gentile or a Jew —
we clear the pile from on top of him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer from step 2 as already known.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that שמואל teaches we may carry a knife through רשות הרבים to save the baby.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rockslide משנה already teaches that we break שבת even when it is unsure that a life will be saved, so שמואל's ruling repeats it.

steps.title: An unborn baby never had a חזקה of life
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rockslide victim was known to be alive before, but the unborn baby never had that status, so we might have thought we do not break שבת for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: there, the person was known to be alive before; but here, where the baby never had that status from the start, we do not break שבת. So שמואל teaches us that we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל's ruling is still needed. The baby case is weaker than the rockslide case, so we could not learn it from there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man under the rubble had a חזקה of being alive before the collapse, which supports assuming he is still alive. A baby not yet born never had such a חזקה. שמואל teaches that we break שבת even so.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (a mistaken first thought)
a presumed status of being alive

steps.whatToRemember: We break שבת to possibly save even an unborn baby, though it never had a חזקה of being alive.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ חֲזָקָה דְּחַיּוּתָא,
phrases.english: it is there that he had a presumption of being alive,
phrases.notes: "There" means the rockslide case: before the collapse, he was known to be alive.

phrases.english: but here, where he did not have
a presumption of being alive from the start —
phrases.notes: "Here" is the unborn baby, who was never yet born alive.

phrases.english: I might say no; so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by showing a difference between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: one had a חזקה of life, the other did not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe we break שבת out of doubt only for someone who was known to be alive before.
steps.terutzMaskana: We break שבת even for an unborn baby who never had a חזקה of being alive.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about an executed woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה: a woman who was executed, whose hair may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A woman who was killed, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה. This line is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that if a woman was executed by בית דין, one may benefit from her hair. The "etc." points back to that full ruling. Now the גמרא will examine it.

keyTerms.meaning: was killed (here, executed by בית דין)
and so on (the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: A woman who was killed, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה says one may benefit from her hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may benefit from the hair of a woman who was executed.

steps.title: But a dead body is forbidden for benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why her hair is allowed, since a dead body, hair included, is forbidden for any benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? They are forbidden for benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling. A dead body is אסור בהנאה, so how can we use her hair?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hair is treated as part of the body. Since a corpse is forbidden for benefit, her hair should be too. The משנה's permission seems to clash with this rule.

phrases.english: But why? They are items forbidden for benefit!
phrases.notes: "They" means her body and hair; a dead body may not be used for any benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one may benefit from an executed woman's hair.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dead body and its hair are אסור בהנאה, so benefit should be forbidden.

steps.title: She asked to give her hair to her daughter
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the משנה is talking about a woman who said before she died: give my hair to my daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is where she says, "Give my hair to my daughter."
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The משנה is about a woman who asked that her hair be given to her daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב suggests that her request makes the hair usable. The case is no longer any executed woman, only one who made this request. The next step will question whether a request can really do that.

keyTerms.meaning: in a case where she says

phrases.english: Rav said:
Where she says, "Give my hair to my daughter."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case of the משנה to a woman who made a request.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow any executed woman's hair, against the rule that a corpse is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a woman who asked that her hair be given to her daughter.

steps.title: Would we give her hand if she asked?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: if she said to give her hand to her daughter, surely we would not do it, so her request cannot make the hair allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she said, "Give my hand to my daughter," would we give it to her?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's answer. A person's wish cannot permit a forbidden body part, as her hand shows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her request could permit the hair, it should also permit her hand. But clearly we would not give the hand. So the request alone cannot explain why the hair is allowed.

phrases.english: If she had said, "Give my hand to my daughter,"
would we give it to her?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's answer that her request makes the hair allowed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her request could not permit her hand, so it should not permit her hair either.

steps.title: רב says the hair is a wig
steps.stepSummary: רב gives a new answer: the משנה means a פאה נכרית (wig). It is allowed only because she said 'give it'; without that, it counts as her body and is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The משנה is talking about a wig. The גמרא infers: the reason it is allowed is that she said 'give it.' But if she did not say 'give it,' it is part of her body and is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: After the hand question knocked down the first answer, רב explains that the 'hair' in the משנה is really a wig. The גמרא then reads an inference from his words, which sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wig is not truly part of her body, so her words 'give it to my daughter' can make it a separate object that may be used. That solves the hand problem from step 8, because a hand truly is her body. But the inference is that a wig she is wearing, with no such words, is treated as part of her body and is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A wig, literally 'foreign hair', hair that did not grow on her own head
'The reason is because...', used to draw an inference from a ruling
'But if not...', the opposite case that follows from the inference

phrases.english: Rav said: It is about a wig,
the reason is that she said 'give,'
but if she did not say 'give' —
it is her body, and it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 8 knocked down by redefining the hair as a wig.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (real hair becomes a wig)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means her real hair, which her words could not permit, just as with a hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a wig, which her words 'give it' can separate from her body; without those words, a worn wig counts as her body.

steps.title: רבי יוסי was unsure whether a wig counts as the body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא asked about the hair of righteous women, and רבא said he meant a wig. So it was an open question, not clear that a wig counts as her body.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא was unsure about this! He asked: What is the law about the hair of righteous women? And רבא said: He was asking about a wig.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the inference from step 9. It brings a question from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא showing that whether a wig counts as the body was left undecided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From רב it sounds obvious that a wig is her body unless she said otherwise. But רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא treated the same wig question as a real doubt, and רבא confirmed he meant a wig. Something cannot be both obvious and an open question.

keyTerms.meaning: He was unsure about it; it was an open question for him
'What is the law?', the way a question is asked

phrases.english: But wasn't it a question for
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina,
as Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina asked:
The hair of righteous women — what is the law?
phrases.notes: His question is about a city that went after עבודה זרה, where property is burned: does her hair count as property or as her body?

phrases.english: And Rava said: It is about a wig.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference drawn from רב's answer in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a worn wig is clearly her body unless she said 'give'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, as explained by רבא, treated the status of a wig as an open question, so it cannot be clear that a wig is her body.

steps.title: A wig on a peg versus a wig she is wearing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא was unsure only about a wig hanging on a peg. Here, the wig is attached to her, so it clearly counts as her body unless she said 'give.'
steps.simpleTranslation: No. When רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא was unsure, it was about a wig hanging on a peg. Here, the wig is attached to her. So the reason it is allowed is that she said 'give,' but if she did not say 'give,' it is her body and is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by saying the two cases are different wigs: one hanging on a peg, one being worn. This keeps רב's answer standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wig on a peg is not on her, so it is unclear whether it is part of her person or just her property. A wig she is wearing is attached to her, so it is treated as her body. Only her words 'give it' can change that, which is exactly what רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: That is hanging on a peg
A peg or nail on the wall
That is attached to her, being worn

steps.whatToRemember: A wig being worn counts as the woman's body unless she said 'give it to my daughter.' The open question of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא was only about a wig hanging on a peg.

phrases.english: No, he was not unsure about that;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: when Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina was unsure,
it was where it hangs on a peg.
Here, where it is attached to her,
the reason is that she said 'give,'
but if she did not say 'give' —
it is her body, and it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats רב's inference from step 9, now showing it still holds.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא דִּתְלֵי בְּסִיכְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by separating the two wig cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases (a wig on a peg versus a wig being worn)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's doubt covers every wig, including one being worn, which would clash with רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: His doubt is only about a wig on a peg; a worn wig is her body unless she said 'give,' just as רב said.

steps.title: The woman is compared to the animal, so it must mean her real hair
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רב: the משנה lists the woman next to the animal, and with the animal it means its own body, so with the woman it must mean her own hair too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק found רב's answer difficult. The משנה teaches the woman's case just like the animal's case. With the animal, it means its own body. So with the woman, it must also mean her own body, not a wig.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב נחמן בר יצחק, attacks רב's idea that the משנה is talking about a wig.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts the woman's case right next to the executed animal. With the animal, the ruling is about its own body. So the parallel suggests the woman's case is also about her own body, meaning her real hair, and רב's wig reading does not fit.

phrases.aramaic: קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: It was difficult for Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
But it teaches [the woman's case] similar to the animal's case!
Just as there, it means its own body,
so too here, it means her own body!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wig explanation that steps 9 and 11 had just defended.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's explanation that the משנה's 'hair' means a wig
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה draws a parallel to the animal, whose case is clearly about its own body. So the woman's case must also be about her own body.

steps.title: Death forbids the woman, but the verdict forbids the animal
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the משנה about real hair: the woman becomes forbidden only when she dies, but the animal becomes forbidden as soon as it is sentenced.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said: The woman becomes forbidden through her death. The animal becomes forbidden through its final verdict.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives his own answer to why the woman's hair is allowed and the animal's hair is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are about real hair. The animal is forbidden from the moment of its verdict, while it is still alive, so the hair growing on it becomes forbidden too. The woman is only forbidden once she dies. Her hair does not change at death, so it stays allowed.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said:
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן בר יצחק from the step before.

phrases.english: This one, her death makes her forbidden,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the woman.

phrases.english: and that one, its final verdict makes it forbidden.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having rejected the wig reading, he offers a different explanation of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on when each one becomes forbidden
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman's hair must be a wig, since real hair from a forbidden body should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is real hair. The animal is forbidden at its verdict, while alive. The woman is forbidden only at death, which does not affect her hair.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches: רב says the hair is a wig, which is allowed only if she said 'give'. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is real hair, because the woman becomes forbidden only at death, while the animal is forbidden from its verdict.

steps.title: לוי has a teaching for each side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that לוי taught a ברייתא supporting רב and another supporting רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי taught a ברייתא like רב, and לוי taught a ברייתא like רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces two supporting ברייתות and will now quote them one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each approach gets backing from a ברייתא taught by לוי. Nothing is proven yet in this line. It just tells us what is coming.

phrases.english: Levi taught [a ברייתא] in line with Rav,

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי לֵוִי כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק.
phrases.english: and Levi taught [a ברייתא] in line with Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two approaches are set out, it introduces support for both.
steps.raayaObject: Both רב's view and רב נחמן בר יצחק's view

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא that matches רב
steps.stepSummary: Levi's ברייתא: if a woman going to her execution says to give her hair to her daughter, we give it. If she died without saying so, we do not, because a dead body is forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי taught like רב: A woman who is going out to be executed and says, 'Give my hair to my daughter' — we give it. If she died without saying this, we do not give it, because a dead person is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first ברייתא, the one that supports רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as רב said, the ברייתא makes the difference depend on whether she said 'give'. If she did not say it, the item is forbidden because of the איסור הנאה of a dead body.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden to get any benefit from

phrases.english: Levi taught in line with Rav:
A woman who is going out to be executed
and said: 'Give my hair to my daughter' —
we give it.
If she died [without saying this], we do not give it,
because a dead body is forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first of the two promised ברייתות, the one for רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the hair is allowed only if she said 'give'
steps.raayaSupportSource: לוי's ברייתא about the woman going to be executed

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to tell us that a dead body is forbidden for benefit, since everyone knows that.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for seeming to teach something everyone already knows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a dead body is forbidden for benefit. So if the ברייתא were only about her own hair, it would be teaching nothing new. There must be a new point here.

phrases.english: It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the last line of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ending: 'because a dead body is forbidden for benefit'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא should not teach something already known.

steps.title: Even a dead person's adornments are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is really about a wig, and it teaches that even the adornments of a dead person are forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means that the adornments of a dead person are forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's new point is about adornments, like a wig, not about the body itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that things attached to her as decoration, like a wig, count as part of the dead body and are forbidden. This is exactly רב's wig explanation, so the ברייתא does support רב.

keyTerms.meaning: The adornments of a dead person (like a wig)

steps.whatToRemember: Levi's ברייתא supports רב: a wig attached to a dead woman counts as an adornment of the dead and is forbidden, unless she said 'give it' before she died.

phrases.english: Rather, [it teaches] that the adornments of a dead person are forbidden for benefit.
phrases.notes: Here the 'hair' in the ברייתא means a wig, just as רב explained.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by showing the ברייתא's new point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (wig instead of real hair)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is only repeating that a dead body is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches the new point that a dead person's adornments are forbidden, which supports רב's wig reading.

steps.title: A second ברייתא supports רב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a woman's hair may be used, but an executed animal is forbidden, because death forbids the woman while the verdict forbids the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא agrees with רב נחמן בר יצחק: if a woman dies, her hair may be used, but an animal that was put to death is forbidden for any benefit. What is the difference? For the woman, her death makes her forbidden. For the animal, the court's verdict makes it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב נחמן בר יצחק said: a woman becomes forbidden at death, but an animal becomes forbidden at the verdict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13, רב נחמן בר יצחק answered the question by separating a woman from an animal. This ברייתא states the same split openly. The woman becomes forbidden only at death, which does not change her hair, so her hair stays permitted. The condemned animal is forbidden from the moment it is sentenced, while it is still alive, so its hair is forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden for any benefit or use

steps.whatToRemember: A person becomes forbidden for benefit only at death. A condemned animal becomes forbidden as soon as the court sentences it.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in agreement with רב נחמן בר יצחק:
A woman who died: one may benefit from her hair,
an animal that was put to death is forbidden for benefit;
And what is the difference between this and that?
This one: her death makes her forbidden,
and that one: its verdict makes it forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא for רב was explained in Steps 15 to 17, this brings the promised ברייתא for רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's split: a woman becomes forbidden at death, and an animal becomes forbidden at its verdict.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא, the one announced in Step 14 as taught by לוי.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הכל מעריכין
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of ערכין ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הכל מעריכין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the first פרק of the מסכת. It is not part of any argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learners traditionally say this line when they finish a פרק. It shows their wish to come back and learn it again. A new פרק starts right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, said when finishing a פרק
"Everyone may pledge an ערך," the name of the first פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Everyone may pledge an ערך."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of ערכין is complete.

steps.title: New משנה: an ערך is never less than one סלע or more than fifty
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets the lowest and highest payment for an ערך and shows what happens if a poor person who paid later becomes rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person is never charged less than a סלע for an ערך, and never more than fifty סלעים. How does this work? If he gave one סלע and later became rich, he gives nothing more. If he gave less than a סלע and later became rich, he must give fifty סלעים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה that sets the smallest and largest amounts anyone pays for an ערך. It then shows how the smallest amount works for a poor person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor person pays only what he can afford, but at least one סלע. If he paid a full סלע, he has finished his obligation, and getting rich later changes nothing. If he paid less than a סלע, nothing counted, so once he is rich he owes the full ערך.

keyTerms.meaning: Are charged for an ערך, a pledge of a person's set value
A silver coin, the same as the שקל of the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Paying less than a סלע does not count as a partial payment. It counts as nothing at all, so the full ערך is still owed once he becomes rich.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One is not charged for an ערך less than a סלע,
and not more than fifty סלעים.
How so? If he gave one סלע and then became rich,
he gives nothing more,
if he gave less than a סלע and then became rich,
he gives fifty סלעים.
phrases.notes: Fifty is the highest ערך, so it stands here for the full amount he pledged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ערך payment is never less than one סלע and never more than fifty. One סלע fully frees a poor person, but less than a סלע frees him from nothing.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about a poor person who has five סלעים
steps.stepSummary: If a poor person has five סלעים, רבי מאיר says he gives one and the חכמים say he gives all five. The משנה then repeats its main rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had five סלעים, רבי מאיר says he gives only one, and the חכמים say he gives all of them. One is not charged for an ערך less than a סלע, and not more than fifty.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a מחלוקת about a poor person who owns five סלעים, which is less than his full ערך. Then it repeats its opening rule as a summary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that one סלע, the minimum, is enough even if he owns more. The חכמים hold that a poor person must give everything he has. Both agree he never pays more than his full ערך.

keyTerms.meaning: Five סלעים, the amount he owns in this case

steps.whatToRemember: There is a minimum of one סלע and a maximum of fifty. רבי מאיר says a poor person pays the minimum, and the חכמים say he pays everything he has.

phrases.english: If he had five סלעים in his possession,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ נוֹתֵן אֶלָּא אַחַת,
phrases.english: רבי מאיר says: he gives only one,
and the חכמים say: he gives all of them.
One is not charged for an ערך less than a סלע,
and not more than fifty סלעים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a disputed case and then restates the main rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poor person with five סלעים: רבי מאיר says he pays one, and the חכמים say he pays all five. The range always stays between one and fifty סלעים.

steps.title: Where do we learn that an ערך is never less than one סלע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that an ערך is never less than a סלע and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'An ערך is never less than a סלע.' How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It quotes the first rule and asks where it comes from in the Torah. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a minimum payment of one סלע but no source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: How do we know this? A request for a source

phrases.english: Gemara: One is not valued at less than a sela.
From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the משנה from step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the Torah for the minimum ערך of one סלע.

steps.title: The source for the minimum is the word שקל
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'every ערך shall be in the שקל of the Sanctuary' teaches that no ערך is less than one שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And every ערך of yours shall be according to the שקל of the Sanctuary.' This means: every ערך that you set may not be less than one שקל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. It reads the word 'שקל' as setting the lowest possible payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links every ערך to the שקל. The גמרא reads that as a floor: no ערך, even for a very poor person, may go below one שקל, which is one סלע.

keyTerms.meaning: your valuation, the fixed amount set by the Torah
the שקל of the Sanctuary, equal to a סלע

phrases.english: As it is written: "And all your valuations
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:25

phrases.english: shall be according to the shekel of the Sanctuary,"
all valuations that you assess
shall not be less than a shekel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ' sets one שקל as the lowest ערך.
steps.whyThisMatters: This same פסוק is used again below, both in רבי מאיר's reasoning and in the רבנן's answer.

steps.title: The source for the maximum is the word 'fifty'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's rule that an ערך is never more than fifty סלעים comes from the פסוק that says 'fifty'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not more than fifty סלעים.' As it is written: 'fifty'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next rule of the משנה and gives its source right away. The Torah's highest ערך is fifty שקלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists different ערכים by age and gender, and the highest one is fifty שקלים for a man aged twenty to sixty. So no ערך can ever go above fifty, even for a rich person.

keyTerms.meaning: fifty סלעים, the highest ערך in the Torah

phrases.english: Nor more than fifty sela.
As it is written: "Fifty."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יָתֵר עַל חֲמִשִּׁים סְלָעִים. דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the minimum, the גמרא now gives the source for the maximum.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'fifty' in the Torah is the highest ערך.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר say the poor person pays only one סלע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a poor person with five סלעים and asks for רבי מאיר's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he had five סלעים, etc.' What is the reason of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the argument in the משנה from step 21. It asks why רבי מאיר lets him pay just one סלע even though he has five. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems strange that a person with five סלעים may pay only one. The גמרא wants the source that leads רבי מאיר to this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: in his possession, what he owns

phrases.english: If there were five in his possession, etc.
What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the minimum and maximum to the argument in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי מאיר's ruling that a poor person with five סלעים pays only one.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: either fifty or one שקל
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר sees two amounts in the Torah, 'fifty' and 'שקל', and reads them as two choices: the full ערך or one שקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'fifty', and it is written 'שקל'. So it is either fifty or one שקל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי מאיר. The Torah mentions two amounts, so he says there are only two options: the full amount, or one שקל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר there is no middle amount. A person who cannot pay the full ערך drops straight down to one שקל, even if he owns five. So he pays one סלע.

phrases.english: It is written "fifty," and it is written "shekel,"
phrases.notes: These are the two פסוקים from steps 23 and 24.

phrases.english: either fifty or a shekel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 using the two פסוקים from steps 23 and 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר reads 'fifty' and 'שקל' as the only two choices, so a poor person pays one שקל.

steps.title: The רבנן: שקל is only a minimum, and a person who can pay more must pay more
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the word שקל only sets the minimum. A different פסוק, 'according to the means of the one who vowed', makes a person who can afford more pay more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? That פסוק comes to teach that every ערך you set may not be less than a שקל. But where he has more, the פסוק says: 'according to the means of the one who vowed', and here he does have the means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן read the word שקל that רבי מאיר used. They answer that it only sets a minimum, and they bring a different פסוק that requires paying more when he can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not deny the פסוק of שקל. They limit it: it is a floor, not one of only two choices. The פסוק 'אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנּוֹדֵר' ties the payment to what he can afford, so a person with five סלעים pays all five.

keyTerms.meaning: that is what it comes to teach
what his hand can reach, meaning what he can afford
the one who made the vow

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן agree that the minimum is one שקל. They only disagree about whether a person who has more may still pay just one.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: 'fifty' and 'שקל' are the only two choices, so he pays one. רבנן: שקל is just a minimum, and 'אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנּוֹדֵר' makes him pay all he can, up to the full ערך.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? That verse,
phrases.notes: He means: how do the רבנן deal with the word 'שקל' that רבי מאיר relies on?

phrases.english: that all valuations that you assess

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהוּ פְּחוּתִים מִשְׁקָל הוּא דַּאֲתָא,
phrases.english: shall not be less than a shekel, that is what it comes for,
where he has more —
the verse states: "According to the means of him that vowed,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:8

phrases.english: and here he has the means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reading of the same פסוק that רבי מאיר used in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the רבנן, the word שקל sets only a minimum, and 'אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנּוֹדֵר' requires a person who can afford more to pay more.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the root of the argument in the משנה: whether the Torah gives two fixed choices or a scale based on what the person can afford.

steps.title: What does רבי מאיר do with the פסוק about means?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר uses the פסוק 'according to the means of the one who vowed', since the רבנן used it for their own rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, what does he do with that פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי מאיר and asks what he learns from the פסוק that the רבנן just used. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27 the רבנן learned from 'according to the means of the one who vowed' that a person who can afford more pays more. רבי מאיר does not hold that rule, so the פסוק must be teaching him something else. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר?
phrases.notes: Short for: what does רבי מאיר do with the פסוק 'according to the means of the one who vowed'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side reads the פסוק the רבנן just used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי מאיר learns from 'according to the means of the one who vowed'.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the vower's means count, not the means of the person being valued
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר uses the פסוק to teach that we look at the means of the person who made the vow, not the means of the person whose ערך was vowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק comes to teach: the means of the one who vows, and not the means of the one whose value was vowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי מאיר, the פסוק teaches whose wealth matters. It is the wealth of the person who made the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people can be involved in an ערך vow: the one who vows, and the one whose ערך is vowed. The פסוק says 'the means of the one who vowed', so the vower's money decides the payment. רבי מאיר uses the פסוק only for this point, so he does not learn from it that a richer person pays more.

keyTerms.meaning: The means of the person who makes the vow
The means of the person whose value was vowed

phrases.english: That verse: 'the means of the one who vows,'
and not the means of the one whose value was vowed
is what it comes for.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יַד הַנּוֹדֵר וְלֹא יַד הַנִּידָּר הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי מאיר, the פסוק teaches that the vower's means decide the payment, not the means of the person being valued.

steps.title: The רבנן: the same פסוק also teaches that more means means paying more
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that once the פסוק says the vower's means count, it follows on its own that someone who can afford more must pay more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן would say: don't you automatically learn from it that wherever his means reach, we take from him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן can get their rule from the same פסוק. Their rule comes along automatically with רבי מאיר's lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that the vower's means are what count. They say that if his means are what count, then his means also set how much he pays. So the person pays as much as he can afford, up to the full ערך, and not just one שקל.

keyTerms.meaning: He can afford it, his means reach that far

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree the vower's means count. They disagree on whether a vower who can afford more must pay more: the רבנן say yes, and רבי מאיר says one שקל is enough.

phrases.english: And the רבנן would say:
Don't you automatically learn from it
that wherever his means reach,
take from him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the רבנן get their rule from the same reading רבי מאיר uses.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Saying the vower's means count also means a vower who can afford more pays more.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: two ערך vows paid with five סלעים
steps.stepSummary: A man with five סלעים vowed his ערך twice, then paid four for the second vow and one for the first. He has paid both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: If someone had five סלעים, said 'my ערך is on me', then said again 'my ערך is on me', and gave four to the second vow and one to the first, he has paid both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב אדא בר אהבה that follows the רבנן's view about paying by one's means. A man pays two ערך vows using only five סלעים in total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the רבנן, a person pays as much as he can afford. Here it seems he could afford five, so you would expect him to owe five for each vow. Yet רב אדא says paying four and then one covers both vows, and the order of payment is what makes it work.

keyTerms.meaning: 'My ערך is upon me', a vow to give one's own Torah value to the Temple
Silver coins, the same as the שקל of the Sanctuary

steps.confusionAlert: He pays the second vow FIRST (four סלעים) and the first vow LAST (one סלע). If he paid them in the normal order, the result would not work this way.

phrases.english: רב אדא בר אהבה said:
If he had five סלעים in his possession,
and said, 'My ערך is upon me,'
and then said again, 'My ערך is upon me,'
and he gave four to the second vow
and one to the first vow,
he has fulfilled both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the רבנן's rule about paying by one's means to a tricky case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Paying four for the second ערך and one for the first ערך, out of five סלעים, covers both vows.

steps.title: Why does this work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why paying four and then one is enough for both vows. This question sets up the explanation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems he could afford five, so he should owe five on each vow. The גמרא needs to explain how he got away with paying less.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why five סלעים, split four and one, cover two ערך vows.

steps.title: A later creditor who collected first keeps what he took
steps.stepSummary: The answer starts with a known rule: if a creditor whose loan came later collects before the earlier creditor, he keeps what he collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: A later creditor who got there first and collected, what he collected he has collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a rule from the laws of debts to explain the case. This is the first half of the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an earlier creditor comes first. But once a later creditor has actually collected, we do not take the money back from him. In our case the second vow is like the later creditor, and it collected first.

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor whose loan came later

phrases.english: A later creditor
who got there first and collected,
what he collected, he has collected.
phrases.notes: The second vow is like the later creditor, since it was paid before the first vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל חוֹב מְאוּחָר שֶׁקָּדַם וְגָבָה מַה שֶּׁגָּבָה גָּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the general rule behind the ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The payment to the second vow stands, just as a later creditor who collected first keeps what he took.

steps.title: At each payment he counts as poor
steps.stepSummary: When he paid the second vow, his money was tied up for the first vow, so he counted as poor. When he paid the first vow, he only had one סלע left.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he gave to the second, his money was tied up for the first. When he gave to the first, he had nothing more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the rule to the case and shows that at each payment the man counts as poor. So small amounts are enough for both vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While paying the second vow, all his money was tied up for the first vow, so for the second vow he counts as having nothing. He pays as a poor person, and the four he gave is more than enough. Then for the first vow he really has only one סלע left, so one סלע is all he must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Tied up, owed for an earlier debt

steps.whatToRemember: Under the רבנן, the amount owed depends on what a person has when he pays. By paying the later vow first, he counts as poor for both vows.

phrases.english: At the time he gave to the second vow,
his money was tied up for the first vow.
At the time he gave to the first vow,
he had nothing more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the creditor rule to the case of the two vows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At each payment the man counts as poor, first because of the tie to the first vow and then because only one סלע remains, so four plus one covers both vows.
